value.rationale: A complete and sharp classification of the first two possible complementary-orbit sparsity ranks throughout a natural two-prime-support exponent-square family. The singleton square-root orbit makes n=36 an exceptional boundary, and the proof shows a genuine rank gap for every other parameter pair. This complements current classification efforts for sparse strongly pseudoperfect representations, without claiming a downstream theorem or a complete census.
